text:
marie: Heads up — found a subtle duplicate-side-effect during onboarding sample runs. It happens when a streaming request experiences auth rotation + a 429, and our retry path effectively re-emits the final completion event. Short repro below.

ton y: hmm that combo rings a bell. is it because we re-issue a fresh HTTP request and lose request-scoped metadata?

marie: Exactly. Our streaming resume logic reconstructs the outgoing request and some SDKs don't carry over the ephemeral request metadata (headers or replay ids). The consumer webhook sees two completion posts for the same logical event.

yael: Can you paste a minimal log trace?

marie: Sure:```
2025-01-07T09:41:02Z INFO request=start id=req-44
2025-01-07T09:41:03Z INFO auth:refresh triggered for tenant=acme
2025-01-07T09:41:03Z WARN upstream=429 id=req-44
2025-01-07T09:41:03Z INFO sdk:retry id=req-44 attempt=2 backoff=150ms
2025-01-07T09:41:04Z INFO webhook POST /events event=completion id=evt-22 status=200
2025-01-07T09:41:04Z INFO webhook POST /events event=completion id=evt-22 status=200 (duplicate)
```

tony: So two things to fix: (A) preserve a stable replay id across the request lifecycle, (B) make retry/backoff for 429 safer for streaming.

yael: Proposal: SDK generates X-RW-Replay at request start and keeps it immutable. Expose sdk.ctx.replay_id to apps. For streaming resume, include an optional X-RW-Resume-Offset header when we can resume instead of full restart.

raul: Can we just push idempotency responsibility to the sampleapp (set X-Idempotency-Key on outgoing webhook posts)? That seems less invasive.

marie: We should do both. Relying on app authors is fragile during onboarding — new users won't think about token rotations. SDK default reduces surprise. Also doc/update sampleapp to mirror replay_id into X-Idempotency-Key.

tony: For 429 backoff: use decorrelated jitter (FullJitter/Erlang style) with an upper cap. Important: for streaming requests prefer resume-first (short window) and only fall back to full retry after N resume failures.

yael: Agree. Also: test matrix across SDKs. Node and Python have a single request object we can mutate; Go reconstructs requests in goroutines so needs a small change to thread a metadata token through.

marie: Draft API sketch for Node SDK:```js
// request lifecycle
const ctx = { replayId: uuidv4(), preserveReplay: true }
await sdk.generate(input, { ctx })
// inside sampleapp handler
const replay = req.sdkContext?.replayId
fetch(CONSUMER_URL, { headers: { 'X-Idempotency-Key': replay } })
```

raul: Telemetry wise: emit boolean flags: `sdk.replay.generated` and `sdk.replay.preserved_on_retry`. We'll need a metric to catch regressions.

tony: Test plan: e2e harness that simulates: a) token rotation mid-stream, b) inject 429 on first retry, c) ensure consumer receives exactly one completion event with the idempotency key. Add unit tests for header-preservation in the retry wrapper.

yael: Parity checklist: Node ✅ (small change), Python ✅ (single request object), Go 🔧 (refactor goroutine request build to accept ctx). I can take Go.

marie: Docs: quickstart troubleshooting note + code snippet showing how to echo replay id into consumer headers. Also add FAQ entry: "Why did I get duplicate webhook events?"

ci-bot: ci:job #1210 flaky sampleapp webhook tests detected. Details: https://ci.example.com/1210

raul: One gotcha: some environments strip unknown headers (proxies, cloud functions). Recommend apps mirror X-RW-Replay into `X-Idempotency-Key` when calling external consumers. Add that to docs.

tony: Edge-case: long-running streams with many resume attempts. We should expire the replay id after some time/attempts to avoid infinite dedupe windows; maybe TTL=5m or attempts<=5. Document behavior.

yael: Good call. Add config: `replayTtlMs` and `maxReplayAttempts`. Defaults: 300000ms, 5 attempts. Make configurable.

marie: I'll open PRs: SDK changes (Node, Python, Go), sampleapp mirrors idempotency, docs + e2e harness. Title: "ensure stable replay id across retries + sampleapp idempotency examples"

raul: Thanks — lmk if you want help with the e2e harness. I can add the flaky-network library and a CI gate.

marie: Will do. I'll post PR links here. :shipit:
